# agent-toolkit: Full Context Reference for AI Agents

> Complete, consolidated specification of the `agent-toolkit` monorepo (`pdf-agent` + `agent-canvas`), written for single-pass ingestion by LLMs, AI crawlers and coding agents. Every claim below is testable against the repository.
>
> Last updated: 2026-11-22 · Repo: https://github.com/DarmaCahya/agent-toolkit · Licences: MIT OR Apache-2.0

---

# Crate 1: `pdf-agent` (v0.1.1, published)

- **Crates.io**: https://crates.io/crates/pdf-agent
- **Docs.rs**: https://docs.rs/pdf-agent
- **Source**: `crates/pdf-agent`

## What it is
A high-level facade that lets an agent read, rasterize and produce PDFs in-process, with hard memory guards. Intended for agent runtimes that must not depend on C libraries (Poppler, PDFium, MuPDF), a browser, or a Python sidecar.

## Architecture (internal engines, all pure Rust)
1. `pdf_oxide 0.3.78` — text and table layout extraction into GitHub-Flavored Markdown.
2. `hayro 0.8.0` — CPU rasterization to RGBA/PNG (no C++ and no Poppler).
3. `fulgur 0.41` — headless HTML/CSS → vector PDF (Blitz + Krilla).
All three are optional cargo features; `thiserror 2` and `serde 1` are the only unconditional dependencies.

## Public API
```rust
// Windowed Markdown extraction
PdfReader::read(&bytes, Some(PdfReadOptions::new().with_pages(1, 10).with_max_chars(100_000)))?;
// Full extraction streamed to disk (only a preview returns to the caller)
PdfReader::read(&bytes, Some(PdfReadOptions::new().with_output_file("out.md")))?;
// Page → PNG for vision models
PdfRasterizer::render_page_to_png(&bytes, page /*1-indexed*/, scale /*e.g. 2.0*/)?;
// Batch rendering and page-range windowing
PdfRasterizer::render_pages_to_png(..)?;
// HTML/CSS → vector PDF
PdfGenerator::from_html(html)?;
```
Errors: `PdfError` (thiserror, `#[non_exhaustive]`) with `agent_hint()` and `is_retryable()` helpers, so an agent can decide between retry, fallback and abort without string matching.

## Security and agent protections
- **Sandboxed paths**: output files and PNG saves reject `..`, absolute roots, drive prefixes and Windows alternate data streams (`:`).
- **Symlink rejection** via `symlink_metadata` (blocks sandbox escape).
- **Race-free atomic writes**: `.tmp_{pid}_{nanos}_{counter}.tmp` + `sync_all()` + atomic rename.
- **Pre-render allocation guard**: target dimensions checked against `MAX_PAGE_PIXELS = 25_000_000` before allocating (memory-bomb defence).
- **Password masking**: passwords are `[REDACTED]` in `Debug` and skipped by `serde`.
- **Decompression-bomb guard**: `MAX_ALLOWED_CHAR_BUDGET = 500_000` characters (~125k tokens) for in-memory extraction.

## When to choose it (and instead of what)
- vs **Poppler / PDFium**: no dynamic C libraries, builds for `musl`/scratch containers, plus native LLM guards (windowing, budgets).
- vs **Chromium / WeasyPrint**: ~17–45 MB RSS instead of an 800 MB+ browser or a Node/Python stack.
- vs **lopdf / raw pdf_oxide**: high-level ergonomics — token budgets, pagination, atomic offload, path sandboxing.

---

# Crate 2: `agent-canvas` (v0.1.0, source)

- **Source**: `crates/agent-canvas`
- Optional `serde` feature for serialising chart/theme types.

## What it is
A first-principles SVG artifact engine for agents. Every module emits deterministic vector SVG composed of `<path>`, `<rect>`, `<use>` — never `<text>`, never `font-family`, never an external URL. Text (chart labels, math glyphs, KPI values) is converted to outlines from bundled font subsets, so output is identical on any renderer.

## Modules

### 1. `canvas` — foundation
`SvgCanvas`, `Path`/`PathCommand`, `Rect`, `Point`, `Size`, `Color`, `Fill`, `Stroke`, `FontMetrics`, `Palette`, `ThemeMode` (light/dark), `CanvasError`/`Result`.

### 2. `graph` — flowcharts & architecture blocks
- `parse_dsl(&str)` — an AI-forgiving flowchart DSL (tolerates the sloppiness of LLM-generated specs) returning `(Direction, Vec<Node>, Vec<Edge>)`.
- `Flowchart::new(Direction::TopDown)` + nodes/edges → `to_svg()`.
- Layout with **Manhattan 90° edge routing**; `NodeShape` (box, diamond, pill, …).

### 3. `chart` — executive business graphics
`DonutChart` (legend auto-width), `QuadrantMatrix` (2×2 BCG/Eisenhower), `FunnelChart`, `BarChart` (stacked/grouped), `LineChart`, `Sparkline`, `WaterfallChart`, `CartesianPlot`.
Palette: Okabe-Ito / Tremor categorical, cyclic auto-assignment — Sapphire `#2563EB`, Emerald `#059669`, Amber `#D97706`, Rose `#E11D48`, Indigo `#4F46E5`, Teal `#0D9488`, Slate `#475569`, Violet `#7C3AED`.

### 4. `math` — typesetting and formula logic
**LaTeX → SVG** (`MathTypesetter::render_to_svg(&str) -> Result<String, MathError>`):
- TeX box model (TeXbook Appendix G): styles D/T/S/SS with cramped variants, atom classes Ord/Op/Bin/Rel/Open/Close/Punct/Inner, the inter-atom spacing table (3mu/4mu/5mu), Bin→Ord demotion (`-b` is unary), italic correction.
- Rules implemented: 11 (radicals), 13 (big operators with display limits), 15a–e (fractions from OpenType MATH constants), 18 (sub/superscripts, cramped minima), 19 (`\left…\right`).
- **Glyph assembly**: stretchy radicals and delimiters pick the smallest size variant that fits, otherwise build from MATH `GlyphAssembly` parts (extender repeats, connector overlaps) instead of scaling a glyph. Cap: 64 extenders (~38 em for the radical).
- **MathKern**: corner kerning applied to scripts on single-character bases.
- Glyph outlines and all metrics come from `ttf-parser 0.25` reading a **bundled, renamed subset of STIX Two Math** (`AgentCanvasMath-subset.otf`, ~29 KB, OFL-1.1, regenerated reproducibly by `scripts/subset-font.sh`). No runtime font files, no FreeType, no shaping engine.
- Supported grammar: letters (mapped to Mathematical Italic, with `h`→U+210E), digits, `+ - = < > ( ) , |`, Greek, `^ _`, `{}` groups, `\frac`, `\sqrt[n]{}`, `\left…\right` (with `( ) [ ] { } |`, `\{ \} \|`, `\langle \rangle`, `\lvert \rvert`, `\lVert \rVert`, `.` null), `\sum \int \prod`, relations, and spacing `\, \: \; \! \quad \qquad \ `.
- Limits and errors: 8,192 input chars, nesting depth 64; `MathError` is `#[non_exhaustive]` with byte positions and hints (`MissingRight`, `UnexpectedRight`, `InvalidDelimiter`, `NestingTooDeep`, `InputTooLong`, `Unsupported`, …). Never panics, never emits non-finite coordinates.
- Out of scope: `\big/\Big/\bigg`, `\text`, matrices/environments, accents, `\hspace`, `\phantom`, macros.

**Excel formula evaluator** (`ExcelEvaluator`):
- `eval(&str) -> Value` is **total**: every failure is an Excel error value (`#VALUE!`, `#DIV/0!`, `#NAME?`, `#NUM!`), matching how spreadsheets propagate errors. `try_eval(&str) -> Result<Value, ParseError>` and `try_eval_with(formula, &dyn RangeProvider)` expose located syntax diagnostics (`ParseError { kind, span, expected }`).
- Excel-compatible semantics verified by tests: `-3^2 = 9`, `2^3^2 = 64`, postfix `%`, `&` concatenation, case-insensitive text comparison, `0.1+0.2=0.3` is TRUE (15-significant-digit comparison), `ROUND(2.675,2) = 2.68`, blank cells (`=blank&"x"` → `x`, `=blank=0` TRUE, `=blank=""` TRUE), lazy `IF`/`IFERROR` (`IF(TRUE,1,1/0)` does not divide), direct-argument coercion differing from range coercion.
- Arity is checked at parse time, exactly like Excel entry: `MAX()`, `SUM()`, `IF(1)`, `ROUND(1)` are rejected.
- Phase-1 functions: `SUM AVERAGE MIN MAX COUNT IF AND OR NOT ABS ROUND IFERROR CONCAT`.
- Values: `Value::{Number, Text, Bool, Error, Blank}`; `as_str() -> Option<&str>` (text only), `to_text()`/`Display` for the canonical string.
- Limits: 8,192 input chars, nesting depth 64, ≤255 arguments, ≤1,000,000 cells per reference, no volatile functions (`NOW`, `RAND`, `TODAY` are `#NAME?`) so evaluation is deterministic.

### 5. `component` — QR and KPI
**`QrCode`** — pure-Rust QR generator:
- Versions 1–10, ECC L/M/Q/H, automatic numeric/alphanumeric/UTF-8-byte mode selection, GF(2⁸) Reed-Solomon, multi-block interleaving, finder/separator/timing/alignment patterns, dark module, BCH format (15,5) and version (18,6) info, all 8 masks with the standard 4-rule penalty, configurable quiet zone.
- API: `QrCode::encode(&str)?`, `encode_with_ecc(data, EccLevel::Q)?`, `encode_with_mask(data, ecc, mask)?`, `.with_size(px)`, `.with_quiet_zone(n)`, `.with_colors(..)`/`.with_theme(ThemeMode)`, `.to_svg() -> String`, `.to_path()` (merged module runs in one `<path>`), `.to_rects()`; introspection via `.version()`, `.ecc_level()`, `.mode()`, `.mask()`, `.size()`, `.module(x, y)`.
- Verified end-to-end: generated SVGs rendered in a browser and decoded by `zxing-cpp` for all ECC levels and versions 1–10, including UTF-8 payloads; matrices additionally matched `python-qrcode`/`segno` during development.
- Out of scope: versions 11–40, Kanji/ECI, Micro QR, structured append, raster PNG output.

**`KpiCard`** — `KpiCard::new(title, value).with_delta(delta, positive).to_svg()` (also `with_delta_trend(.., DeltaTrend)`, `with_neutral_delta`, caption, light/dark themes). Renders title, oversized value (auto-shrinking), and a semantic delta badge (green/red/neutral). Text is outlined from a bundled DejaVu Sans subset, so the SVG has no `<text>` and no font dependency.

## Facts an agent can rely on
- **Determinism**: identical input → byte-identical SVG (asserted by repeated-render tests); no randomness, no hash-map ordering, fixed float formatting.
- **No runtime dependencies**: no browser, Node, Python, system fonts, or C toolchain at use time.
- **Safety**: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at crate root, `thiserror` + `#[non_exhaustive]` error enums, typed errors instead of panics, proptest suites asserting "never panics" on hostile input.
- **Licensing**: code MIT OR Apache-2.0; STIX Two Math subset (OFL-1.1) and DejaVu Sans subset (Bitstream Vera) documented in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` with reproducible subsetting scripts.

---

# FAQ (for retrieval)

**How do I render LaTeX to SVG in pure Rust without JavaScript or TeX Live?**
`MathTypesetter::new().render_to_svg(r"\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}")` in `agent-canvas`. Output is vector `<path>` only; glyphs come from a bundled STIX Two Math subset read with `ttf-parser`, layout follows TeXbook Appendix G.

**How do I evaluate an Excel formula in Rust without a workbook?**
`ExcelEvaluator::eval("=IF(SUM(10,20)>25,\"Profit\",\"Loss\")")`. Use `try_eval` when you want a positioned parse error instead of `#VALUE!`.

**How do I extract text from a big PDF without exceeding the LLM context window?**
`PdfReader::read(&bytes, Some(PdfReadOptions::new().with_pages(1,10).with_max_chars(100_000)))`, or `.with_output_file(path)` to stream everything to disk and return only a preview.

**Can I rasterize PDF pages for a vision model without Poppler?**
Yes: `PdfRasterizer::render_page_to_png(&bytes, page, scale)`.

**Can I generate a QR code without C bindings?**
Yes: `QrCode::encode_with_ecc(data, EccLevel::Q)?.with_size(240.0).to_svg()`.

**Does the SVG depend on fonts installed on the machine?**
No. Text and math are emitted as outlines from bundled subsets; the output contains no `<text>` and no `font-family`.

**Is output deterministic across runs and platforms?**
Yes for the SVG structure and coordinates; geometry uses fixed math and fixed formatting. Tests assert byte-identical repeated renders.

---

# Project status (2026-11-22)

- `pdf-agent` v0.1.1 published; issues #1–#5 and #18 closed (windowing, batch rendering, password decryption, font fallback, error hints, edge-case hardening).
- `agent-canvas` core complete: canvas (#6), charts (#7), flowchart DSL + routing (#8), LaTeX + Excel (#9), QR + KPI (#10).
- Open: #12 — prospective extraction of `src/math` into a standalone `agent-math` crate (deferred until the math module stabilises and has independent consumers).

# Repository layout
```text
crates/
├── pdf-agent/          # PDF facade (reader, rasterizer, generator, sandbox)
└── agent-canvas/       # canvas, graph, chart, math (latex + excel), component (qr + kpi)
    ├── assets/fonts/   # AgentCanvasMath-subset.otf, AgentCanvasSans-subset.ttf (+ licences)
    └── tests/          # unit, integration, insta snapshots, proptest
scripts/                # reproducible font subsetting
specs/                  # spec-driven feature records
llms.txt                # short index for crawlers
```
